Resolves #21636

The current link's lower wave opens into a double helix with short cross-links. Its two filaments pass alternately in front, taper into the ordinary stream at either end, and stay below the label. Hover adds a softer contour to the hovered link. The toolbar's existing route and `aria-current` contract supplies the selection.

![Current header changing from Examples to Learn](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3c61032a106babec6b76b686306cebf402bbb4b4/review-evidence/21636/portal-header.webp?raw=true)

Evidence: L3 (live Portal in Chromium, light and dark, route changes, adjacent hover, reduced motion) → L3 required. No residuals for the visual change. Change class: capability.

## AC Evidence

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `HeaderSelection.spec.mjs` checks active-only geometry, clear, clipping and independent hover. Real route navigation changed the canvas and `aria-current` together; the unmatched Docs route cleared both. |
| AC-2 | [Desktop and compact comparison](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3c61032a106babec6b76b686306cebf402bbb4b4/review-evidence/21636/header-comparison.png?raw=true) in both themes. The short Learn link, wider Examples link, and compact home logo retain clear labels or glyphs. |
| AC-3 | The reduced-motion header held identical pixels over 600 ms and repainted on selection. `HeaderMotion.spec.mjs` covers static invalidation, route/hover updates and the animation lifecycle. |
| AC-4 | Layout and target sizes keep their existing owners. The responsive-header and stored-theme suites passed on the PR head, including 360, 390 and 640 px and desktop. |

## Deltas from ticket

The first pass had smaller, faster twists. A dark phone frame showed the adjacent hover competed with the current route. The final treatment uses wider turns and quieter hover. The existing canvas guide describes the new paint order and hue/shape distinction. On a route change, the connected mark moves on the same frame as `aria-current`. The old link immediately returns to the ordinary stream and the underlying wave keeps its phase. This also keeps a single selected mark during rapid navigation.

## Test Evidence

[Full Examples viewport before](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3c61032a106babec6b76b686306cebf402bbb4b4/review-evidence/21636/page-before.jpg?raw=true) · [Full Examples viewport after](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3c61032a106babec6b76b686306cebf402bbb4b4/review-evidence/21636/page-after.jpg?raw=true) · [Light/dark header detail](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/3c61032a106babec6b76b686306cebf402bbb4b4/review-evidence/21636/header-comparison.png?raw=true)

Frame critique: cross-links across the full button would cut through the lettering. The helix follows the lower strand and the fill tapers inside the selected button. A neighboring hover stays readable without borrowing the selection pattern. Native DevIndex pulse speed and OS reduced motion are independent inputs.

The header and home round table share a window-local CSS motion reader. The Portal browser test changes reduced motion in both directions while the same visible page stays mounted, checking header pixels and the hero frame counter. Removing the worker subscription made it fail. With the subscription restored it passed three consecutive runs. The focused suites passed 141 unit tests and 17 Chromium tests. The [ticket ledger](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21636) records lifecycle and palette fallbacks.
